bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /download-export endpoint concatenated the untrusted filename query parameter directly onto export_path(), checked only file_exists(), and passed the resulting path to response()->download(). A filename such as ../../../../.env therefore escaped storage/app/rconfig/exports and disclosed any existing file readable by the PHP application account; authentication limited who could invoke the endpoint but did not constrain the path.
flaw_origin: Commit 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 created app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php and first wrote download_export() with `$path = export_path() . $_GET['filename']`, followed by file_exists() and response()->download($path), without basename normalization or resolved-path containment. The same commit added export_path(). Commit 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb later exposed that already-flawed method as /download-export inside the auth middleware group; it activated the network attack path but did not write the vulnerable path-handling lines, so it is not the BIC under the protocol.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names author and committer `danielrConfig <daniel@rconfig.com>` and its complete message is only `feat: add file download functionality and export path helper`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/security/advisories/GHSA-m5rw-jcrm-mmwc describes authenticated arbitrary file read through export-download traversal and names 8.2.13 as patched; the assigned global advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6928-5hpx-7r3v. `git log -L 20,36:app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php d133a466^` and `git log -S'$path = export_path() . $_GET[' -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` both trace the raw concatenation/download sequence to 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8. `git show 0813dca...` shows the file created with the vulnerable method, while `git ls-tree 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` returns no entry, directly proving absence in the immediate parent tree. Parent-tree `git grep` finds only a UI link and neither the controller nor export_path(). `git show 5eda5fcf... -- routes/web.php` shows later activation under `Route::group(['middleware' => 'auth'])`. `git cat-file commit 0813dca...` gives one parent, human author/committer danielrConfig, and no trailers, so this is a direct non-merge BIC with nothing to decompose. `git show d133a466...` shows the direct fix: reduce the query value to basename and require realpath-resolved, is_file containment under export_path(), including rejection of symlink escapes. Commit 25d6d2f4314f3c38186d98df9c11da8fe0222862 subsequently refactors the same check into PathContainmentService without reopening the flaw. `git show core-8.2.12^{}:app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` still contains the raw concatenation; `git tag --contains d133a466...` begins at core-8.2.13, and `git show core-8.2.13^{}` resolves the patched release to 72b60a41d9589f3b2e0c5ea0062734b6a0b5a86d. The core-8.2.13 tree uses basename plus PathContainmentService. Although the repository advisory page displays an inconsistent affected expression `<8.2.12`, its patched field says 8.2.13 and the tag trees prove core-8.2.12 vulnerable and core-8.2.13 fixed.
reasoning: The flaw is the unchecked construction and download of a filesystem path, not merely the later route declaration or a later refactor. History follows the exact causal lines: 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 first created them, its immediate parent has no controller file, and later edits retained them until d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee replaced the raw query handling with basename and resolved-path containment. The authenticated route added by 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb completes the exploit lifecycle, and the release trees establish the vulnerable 8.2.12/fixed 8.2.13 boundary. The candidate BIC is a single-parent, focused commit rather than a move, revert, release aggregate, merge, or reconstructable squash. AI attribution is judged only from that BIC's commit object: it has human author/committer identities and no AI marker. The Claude co-author trailer on the later fix commit and the AI trailer on the 8.2.13 release commit are deliberately excluded from BIC attribution. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
